name: Celsius → Fahrenheit
description: Converts a temperature from Celsius to Fahrenheit using c×9/5+32. For example 0°C becomes 32°F and 100°C becomes 212°F.
notes: This converts temperature values, which have an offset of 32; it is not the same as converting a temperature difference (where only ×9/5 applies).

name: Fahrenheit → Celsius
description: Converts a temperature from Fahrenheit to Celsius using (f−32)×5/9. For example 32°F becomes 0°C and 212°F becomes 100°C.
notes: Subtract the 32 offset before scaling. Converting a temperature difference uses only ×5/9, without the −32 term.

name: Celsius → Kelvin
description: Converts a Celsius temperature to the absolute Kelvin scale by adding 273.15. Zero kelvin is absolute zero, the lowest possible temperature.
notes: The scales differ only by the 273.15 offset, so a change of 1°C equals a change of 1 K. Kelvin values below zero are not physical.

name: Miles → km
description: Converts a distance in miles to kilometres by multiplying by 1.609344, the exact number of kilometres in one statute mile.
notes: This uses the international statute mile; nautical miles (1.852 km) are different. The factor 1.609344 is exact by definition.

name: Pounds → kg
description: Converts a mass in pounds to kilograms by multiplying by 0.45359237, the exact number of kilograms in one avoirdupois pound.
notes: This uses the international avoirdupois pound; troy pounds used for precious metals differ. The factor 0.45359237 is exact by definition.

name: Inches → cm
description: Converts a length in inches to centimetres by multiplying by 2.54, the exact number of centimetres in one inch.
notes: The factor 2.54 is exact by international definition. To convert feet, multiply by 12 to get inches first.

name: Kilometers → miles
description: Converts a distance in kilometers to miles by multiplying by 0.621371. One kilometer is a little under two-thirds of a mile.
notes: The factor 0.621371 is the exact reciprocal of 1.609344 km per mile. To convert miles back to kilometers, divide by this factor instead.

name: Kilograms → pounds
description: Converts a mass in kilograms to pounds by multiplying by 2.20462. One kilogram is a little over two pounds.
notes: The factor 2.20462 is the reciprocal of 0.453592 kg per pound. To go from pounds back to kilograms, divide by this factor.

name: Centimeters → inches
description: Converts a length in centimeters to inches by dividing by 2.54, since one inch is defined as exactly 2.54 centimeters. Useful for switching between metric and imperial length units.
notes: The value 2.54 cm per inch is an exact definition, not an approximation. To convert inches back to centimeters, multiply by 2.54 instead.

name: Liters → gallons (US)
description: Converts a volume in liters to US gallons by multiplying by 0.264172. A little under four liters make one US gallon.
notes: This uses the US liquid gallon; the UK (imperial) gallon is larger, about 4.546 liters. To reverse, divide by this factor.

name: Gallons → liters (US)
description: Converts a volume in US gallons to liters by multiplying by 3.78541. One US gallon is a little under four liters.
notes: This assumes the US liquid gallon; the UK imperial gallon converts to about 4.546 liters instead. To reverse, divide by this factor.

name: m/s → km/h
description: Converts a speed in meters per second to kilometers per hour by multiplying by 3.6. This factor comes from 3600 seconds per hour divided by 1000 meters per kilometer.
notes: The 3.6 factor is exact. To convert km/h back to m/s, divide by 3.6 instead.

name: km/h → m/s
description: Converts a speed in kilometers per hour to meters per second by dividing by 3.6. This is the inverse of the m/s to km/h conversion.
notes: The 3.6 factor is exact, from 1000 m per km over 3600 s per hour. To convert m/s back to km/h, multiply by 3.6.

name: Meters → feet
description: Converts a length in meters to feet by multiplying by 3.28084. One meter is a little over three and a quarter feet.
notes: The factor 3.28084 is the reciprocal of the exact 0.3048 m per foot. To convert feet back to meters, divide by this factor.

name: Feet → meters
description: Converts a length in feet to meters by dividing by 3.28084, since one foot equals exactly 0.3048 meters. Useful for changing imperial lengths to metric.
notes: Dividing by 3.28084 is equivalent to multiplying by the exact 0.3048 m per foot. To convert meters back to feet, multiply by 3.28084.

name: km → miles
description: Converts a distance in kilometers to miles by multiplying by 0.621371, the number of miles in one kilometer. For example 10 km equals about 6.21 miles.
notes: This uses the international statute mile; nautical miles differ. The reciprocal factor, about 1.60934, converts miles back to kilometers.

name: m → feet
description: Converts a length in meters to feet by multiplying by 3.28084, the number of feet in one meter. For example 10 meters equals about 32.81 feet.
notes: One foot is exactly 0.3048 meters, so multiply by its reciprocal here. To also get inches, multiply the fractional foot part by 12.

name: feet → m
description: Converts a length in feet to meters by multiplying by 0.3048, the exact number of meters in one foot. For example 10 feet equals 3.048 meters.
notes: The factor 0.3048 is exact by definition of the international foot. Multiply by its reciprocal, about 3.28084, to convert meters back to feet.

name: cm → inches
description: Converts a length in centimeters to inches by multiplying by 0.393701, the number of inches in one centimeter. For example 30 cm equals about 11.81 inches.
notes: One inch is exactly 2.54 centimeters, so this factor is its reciprocal. Multiply inches by 2.54 to convert back to centimeters.

name: mm → inches
description: Converts a length in millimeters to inches by multiplying by 0.0393701 (since one inch equals 25.4 mm). The result gives the same physical length expressed in the imperial unit of inches.
notes: The factor is the reciprocal of 25.4; for an exact conversion use 1/25.4. Input must be in millimeters, not centimeters or meters.

name: yards → m
description: Converts a length in yards to meters by multiplying by 0.9144, which is the exact number of meters in one international yard. The output is the equivalent length in meters.
notes: 0.9144 m per yard is an exact defined value. Do not confuse the yard with the foot (0.3048 m) or with the imperial mile.

name: m → yards
description: Converts a length in meters to yards by multiplying by 1.09361, the reciprocal of 0.9144. The result expresses the same distance in yards.
notes: 1.09361 is a rounded value; for exact results divide by 0.9144. Input is in meters, and the answer is in international yards.

name: nautical miles → km
description: Converts a distance in nautical miles to kilometers by multiplying by 1.852, since one nautical mile is defined as exactly 1852 meters. Nautical miles are used in marine and air navigation.
notes: The nautical mile (1.852 km) differs from the statute land mile (about 1.609 km). It corresponds to one minute of latitude on the Earth.

name: light-years → km
description: Converts a distance in light-years to kilometers by multiplying by about 9.4607×10^12, the distance light travels in a vacuum in one Julian year. It expresses astronomical distances in kilometers.
notes: A light-year is a unit of distance, not time. The factor uses the Julian year (365.25 days); results are astronomically large numbers.

name: feet → inches
description: Converts a length in feet to inches by multiplying by 12, since one foot contains exactly 12 inches. The result is the same length expressed in inches.
notes: This uses the exact 12 inches per foot relation. For a height like 5 ft 6 in, convert only the whole-foot part with this formula and add the extra inches.

name: m → cm
description: Converts a length in meters to centimeters by multiplying by 100, since one meter equals 100 centimeters. This is an exact metric conversion within the SI system.
notes: Simply shifts the decimal point two places. Make sure the input is in meters; using kilometers or millimeters gives a wrong result.

name: kg → pounds
description: Converts a mass in kilograms to pounds by multiplying by 2.20462, the number of avoirdupois pounds in one kilogram. The output is the equivalent mass in pounds.
notes: This converts mass, not weight (force). The pound here is the avoirdupois pound (0.45359237 kg); 2.20462 is its rounded reciprocal.

name: grams → ounces
description: Converts a mass in grams to avoirdupois ounces by multiplying by 0.035274, since one ounce is about 28.35 grams. The result is the same mass expressed in ounces.
notes: This is the avoirdupois ounce (weight), not the fluid ounce (volume). The factor 0.035274 is the reciprocal of 28.3495 g per ounce.

name: ounces → grams
description: Converts a mass in avoirdupois ounces to grams by multiplying by 28.3495, the number of grams in one ounce. The output gives the equivalent mass in grams.
notes: Applies to the avoirdupois ounce of weight, not the fluid ounce of volume. The troy ounce used for precious metals is heavier (about 31.10 g).

name: tonnes → kg
description: Converts a mass in metric tonnes to kilograms by multiplying by 1000, since one tonne equals 1000 kilograms. The result is the same mass expressed in kilograms.
notes: The metric tonne (1000 kg) differs from the US short ton (about 907 kg) and the imperial long ton (about 1016 kg).

name: stone → kg
description: Converts a mass in stone to kilograms by multiplying by 6.35029, since one stone equals 14 pounds or about 6.35 kilograms. The stone is commonly used for body weight in the UK and Ireland.
notes: One stone is exactly 14 pounds. Body weight like 11 st 4 lb must have its pound remainder converted separately and added.

name: kg → stone
description: Converts a mass in kilograms to stone by multiplying by 0.157473, the reciprocal of 6.35029. The result expresses body mass in the stone unit used in the UK and Ireland.
notes: The whole-number part gives stones and the fraction is a portion of 14 pounds, not tens. Multiply the fractional part by 14 to get remaining pounds.

name: gallons → liters
description: Converts a volume in US gallons to liters by multiplying by 3.78541, the number of liters in one US liquid gallon. The output is the equivalent volume in liters.
notes: This is the US gallon; the imperial (UK) gallon is larger at about 4.546 L. Use the correct gallon type for the region.

name: mL → fl oz
description: Converts a volume in milliliters to US fluid ounces by multiplying by 0.033814, since one US fluid ounce is about 29.57 mL. The result is the same volume expressed in fluid ounces.
notes: This is the US fluid ounce; the UK fluid ounce differs (about 28.41 mL). The fluid ounce measures volume, not weight.

name: cups → mL
description: Converts a volume in US cups to milliliters by multiplying by 236.588, the number of milliliters in one US customary cup. It is useful for cooking and recipe conversions.
notes: This uses the US customary cup (236.588 mL); the US legal cup (240 mL) and metric cup (250 mL) differ. Check which cup a recipe intends.

name: liters → pints (US)
description: Converts a volume in liters to US liquid pints by multiplying by 2.11338, since one US pint is about 0.4732 liters. The output is the equivalent volume in US pints.
notes: This is the US liquid pint; the imperial (UK) pint is larger at about 0.568 L, so results differ from British measures.

name: m³ → liters
description: Converts a volume in cubic meters to liters by multiplying by 1000, since one cubic meter equals exactly 1000 liters. This is an exact metric volume conversion.
notes: The factor is exact because a liter is defined as one cubic decimeter. Do not confuse cubic meters with square meters.

name: m² → ft²
description: Converts an area in square meters to square feet by multiplying by 10.7639, which is 1/0.3048 squared. The result expresses the same area in square feet.
notes: The area factor is the square of the length factor (0.3048 m per foot), not the length factor itself. Input must be an area, not a length.

name: ft² → m²
description: Converts an area in square feet to square meters by multiplying by 0.092903, which is 0.3048 squared. The output is the same area expressed in square meters.
notes: The factor is 0.3048^2 because area scales with the square of length. Ensure the input value is an area in square feet.

name: acres → hectares
description: Converts a land area in acres to hectares by multiplying by 0.404686, since one acre is about 0.4047 hectares. The output gives the equivalent area in hectares.
notes: One hectare equals 10,000 square meters, so it holds about 2.47 acres. Both are area units used for land measurement.

name: hectares → acres
description: Converts a land area in hectares to acres by multiplying by 2.47105, the reciprocal of 0.404686. The result expresses the same area in acres.
notes: One hectare (10,000 m²) contains about 2.47 acres. Keep the value as an area; do not apply it to a linear distance.

name: km² → mi²
description: Converts an area in square kilometers to square miles by multiplying by 0.386102, which is 1/1.60934 squared. The output is the same area expressed in square miles.
notes: The area factor equals the square of the length factor (1.60934 km per mile). This uses the statute mile, not the nautical mile.

name: km/h → mph
description: Converts a speed in kilometers per hour to miles per hour by multiplying by 0.621371, the reciprocal of 1.60934. The result is the same speed expressed in mph.
notes: This uses the statute mile. The factor is the same reciprocal used for the km-to-mile length conversion since time cancels out.

name: mph → km/h
description: Converts a speed in miles per hour to kilometers per hour by multiplying by 1.60934, the number of kilometers in one statute mile. The output is the equivalent speed in km/h.
notes: Uses the statute mile, not the nautical mile (which gives knots). The time unit is the same on both sides, so only length is converted.

name: knots → km/h
description: Converts a speed in knots to kilometers per hour by multiplying by 1.852, since one knot is one nautical mile per hour and a nautical mile is 1.852 km. Knots are used in marine and aviation navigation.
notes: A knot is nautical miles per hour, so do not add per hour again. It is faster than the same number of statute mph.

name: mph → m/s
description: Converts a speed in miles per hour to meters per second by multiplying by 0.44704, since one mile is 1609.344 m and one hour is 3600 s. The output is the equivalent speed in SI units.
notes: The factor combines the mile-to-meter conversion with the hour-to-second conversion (1609.344/3600). Uses the statute mile.

name: bar → psi
description: Converts a pressure in bar to pounds per square inch by multiplying by 14.5038, since one bar equals 100,000 pascals. The result is the same pressure expressed in psi.
notes: Bar is a gauge or absolute pressure depending on context; 1 bar is close to but not exactly one atmosphere (1.01325 bar).

name: psi → bar
description: Converts a pressure in pounds per square inch to bar by multiplying by 0.0689476, the reciprocal of 14.5038. The output is the equivalent pressure in bar.
notes: Distinguish gauge pressure (psig) from absolute pressure (psia); the conversion factor is the same but the reference differs. 1 bar equals 100 kPa.

name: atm → pascal
description: Converts a pressure in standard atmospheres to pascals by multiplying by 101325, the exact definition of one standard atmosphere in SI units. The pascal is the SI unit of pressure.
notes: One standard atmosphere is defined as exactly 101,325 Pa, slightly more than 1 bar (100,000 Pa). Not the same as the technical atmosphere (at).

name: mmHg → pascal
description: Converts a pressure in millimeters of mercury to pascals by multiplying by 133.322, since one mmHg (one torr) is about 133.322 Pa. It is often used for blood pressure and vacuum measurements.
notes: One mmHg is essentially equal to one torr. Standard atmospheric pressure is 760 mmHg, which is about 101,325 Pa.

name: kPa → psi
description: Converts a pressure in kilopascals to pounds per square inch by multiplying by 0.145038. Since 1 psi is about 6.895 kPa, the result gives the same pressure in psi.
notes: The factor is 1000 times the pascal-to-psi factor because of the kilo prefix. Standard atmospheric pressure is about 101.3 kPa.

name: joules → calories
description: Converts energy in joules to thermochemical calories by multiplying by 0.239006, the reciprocal of 4.184. The result expresses the same amount of energy in calories.
notes: This is the small gram calorie; the food Calorie (kcal) is 1000 times larger. The thermochemical calorie is defined as exactly 4.184 J.

name: calories → joules
description: Converts energy in thermochemical calories to joules by multiplying by 4.184, the exact definition of one calorie. The joule is the SI unit of energy.
notes: This is the small calorie; multiply food Calories (kcal) by 1000 first. Other calorie definitions (like the IT calorie 4.1868 J) differ slightly.

name: kWh → joules
description: Converts energy in kilowatt-hours to joules by multiplying by 3,600,000, since one kWh is one kilowatt (1000 W) sustained for 3600 seconds. The joule is the SI unit of energy.
notes: The factor is 1000 W times 3600 s. The kilowatt-hour measures energy, not power; power is the rate of energy use.

name: joules → kWh
description: Converts energy in joules to kilowatt-hours by dividing by 3,600,000, the number of joules in one kWh. It expresses energy in the unit used for electricity billing.
notes: Because a kWh is a large amount of energy, joule inputs produce small kWh values. The result measures total energy, not power.

name: BTU → joules
description: Converts energy in British thermal units to joules by multiplying by 1055.06, since one BTU is about 1055 joules. The BTU is common in heating, cooling, and energy ratings.
notes: Several BTU definitions exist; this uses the IT BTU (about 1055.06 J). Do not confuse a BTU with BTU per hour, which is a power rate.

name: hp → watts
description: Converts power in horsepower to watts by multiplying by 745.7, since one mechanical horsepower is about 745.7 watts. The watt is the SI unit of power.
notes: This uses mechanical (imperial) horsepower; metric horsepower (PS) is about 735.5 W. Horsepower measures power, the rate of doing work.

name: watts → hp
description: Converts power in watts to mechanical horsepower by multiplying by 0.00134102, the reciprocal of 745.7. The output expresses power in horsepower.
notes: This gives mechanical horsepower; metric horsepower (PS) uses a slightly different factor. Watts and horsepower both measure power, not energy.

name: kW → hp
description: Converts power in kilowatts to mechanical horsepower by multiplying by 1.34102, since one kilowatt is about 1.341 hp. It is often used for engine and motor ratings.
notes: The factor gives mechanical (imperial) horsepower; metric horsepower (PS) is about 1.3596 per kW. Input is in kilowatts, not watts.

name: newtons → pounds-force
description: Converts a force in newtons to pounds-force by multiplying by 0.224809, since one pound-force is about 4.448 newtons. The result expresses the same force in pounds-force.
notes: Pounds-force is a unit of force, not mass; it is the weight of one pound mass under standard gravity. Do not confuse it with the pound mass.

name: kgf → newtons
description: Converts a force in kilogram-force to newtons by multiplying by 9.80665, the standard gravitational acceleration. One kilogram-force is the weight of one kilogram mass under standard gravity.
notes: The factor is standard gravity (9.80665 m/s²). Kilogram-force is a force unit; do not confuse it with kilogram, which is a mass unit.

name: kelvin → celsius
description: Converts a temperature in kelvin to degrees Celsius by subtracting 273.15. The two scales share the same size of degree, differing only by this offset.
notes: This is a subtraction, not a scale factor, because the scales share the same interval but have different zero points. Zero kelvin is absolute zero.

name: fahrenheit → kelvin
description: Converts a temperature in degrees Fahrenheit to kelvin by subtracting 32, scaling by 5/9, then adding 273.15. This combines the Fahrenheit-to-Celsius step with the Celsius-to-kelvin offset.
notes: Apply the operations in order: subtract 32 first, then multiply by 5/9, then add 273.15. The result is on the absolute kelvin scale.

name: celsius → rankine
description: Converts a temperature in degrees Celsius to degrees Rankine by adding 273.15 to reach kelvin, then multiplying by 9/5. Rankine is an absolute scale with Fahrenheit-sized degrees.
notes: Rankine starts at absolute zero like kelvin but uses Fahrenheit-sized degrees. Add 273.15 before scaling, not after.

name: degrees → radians
description: Converts an angle in degrees to radians by multiplying by pi/180 (about 0.0174533). A full circle of 360 degrees equals 2*pi radians.
notes: The factor is pi/180. Radians are the standard angle unit for trigonometric functions in most math libraries.

name: radians → degrees
description: Converts an angle in radians to degrees by multiplying by 180/pi (about 57.2958). This is the inverse of the degrees-to-radians conversion.
notes: The factor is 180/pi. An input of pi radians gives 180 degrees, and 2*pi radians gives 360 degrees.

name: degrees → gradians
description: Converts an angle in degrees to gradians by multiplying by 1.11111 (10/9), since a full circle is 360 degrees or 400 gradians. Gradians are also called gons.
notes: A right angle is 90 degrees but exactly 100 gradians, which is why the factor is 10/9. Gradians are used in some surveying contexts.

name: MB → GB
description: Converts a data size in megabytes to gigabytes by dividing by 1024, using the binary convention where 1 GB equals 1024 MB. The result is the same amount of data in gigabytes.
notes: This uses the binary 1024 factor (gibibyte convention); decimal SI usage divides by 1000 instead. Confirm which convention applies.

name: GB → MB
description: Converts a data size in gigabytes to megabytes by multiplying by 1024, using the binary convention where 1 GB equals 1024 MB. The output is the same amount of data in megabytes.
notes: This uses the binary 1024 factor; storage makers often use the decimal 1000 instead, so labeled capacities can differ from computed values.

name: GB → TB
description: Converts a storage size in gigabytes to terabytes by dividing by 1024. It answers how many terabytes a given number of gigabytes represents using binary (1024-based) units.
notes: This uses the binary convention where 1 TB = 1024 GB. Drive makers often use decimal units (1 TB = 1000 GB), so results differ from advertised capacities.

name: KB → MB
description: Converts a size in kilobytes to megabytes by dividing by 1024, telling you how many megabytes a given number of kilobytes equals under binary units.
notes: Uses the binary convention 1 MB = 1024 KB. Some contexts use the decimal 1 MB = 1000 KB, which gives a slightly different figure.

name: bytes → bits
description: Converts a number of bytes to bits by multiplying by 8, since one byte consists of 8 bits. It gives the equivalent bit count for a given amount of data.
notes: Assumes the standard 8-bit byte (octet). Data-transfer rates are often quoted in bits per second while file sizes use bytes, so keep the two straight.

name: hours → seconds
description: Converts a duration in hours to seconds by multiplying by 3600, the number of seconds in one hour (60 minutes × 60 seconds).
notes: Straightforward time conversion; the input must be in hours. For mixed hours and minutes, convert each part before adding.

name: days → hours
description: Converts a number of days to hours by multiplying by 24, the number of hours in one day.
notes: Assumes each day is exactly 24 hours. Daylight-saving transitions can make some calendar days 23 or 25 hours long.

name: minutes → seconds
description: Converts a duration in minutes to seconds by multiplying by 60, the number of seconds in one minute.
notes: Simple time conversion; the input must be in minutes. For hours-and-minutes values, convert the hours separately.

name: weeks → days
description: Converts a number of weeks to days by multiplying by 7, the number of days in one week.
notes: Counts calendar days including weekends. If you need only working days, use 5 days per week instead.

name: years → days
description: Converts a number of years to days by multiplying by 365.25, the average length of a year that accounts for leap years.
notes: Uses the average 365.25 days per year, so a specific year may be 365 or 366 days. For exact spans, count actual calendar dates.

name: MPG → L/100km
description: Converts fuel economy from miles per gallon to liters per 100 kilometers by dividing 235.215 by the MPG value. Lower L/100km means better efficiency.
notes: Assumes US gallons; UK (imperial) gallons need a different constant (about 282.5). The two scales are inverse, so higher MPG maps to lower L/100km.

name: L/100km → MPG
description: Converts fuel consumption from liters per 100 kilometers to miles per gallon by dividing 235.215 by the L/100km value. Higher MPG means better fuel economy.
notes: Result is in US MPG; imperial MPG uses a different constant (about 282.5). The relationship is inverse, so lower L/100km yields higher MPG.

name: rpm → Hz
description: Converts rotational speed from revolutions per minute to hertz (revolutions per second) by dividing by 60, since one minute contains 60 seconds.
notes: Hertz here means cycles (revolutions) per second, not angular frequency. To get angular velocity in rad/s, multiply the result by 2π.

name: Hz → rpm
description: Converts frequency in hertz (revolutions per second) to revolutions per minute by multiplying by 60, the number of seconds in one minute.
notes: Treats hertz as revolutions per second. If the value is an angular frequency in rad/s, divide by 2π before applying this conversion.

name: Teaspoons → mL
description: Converts a volume in US teaspoons to millilitres by multiplying by 4.92892, the number of millilitres in one US teaspoon.
notes: Uses the US customary teaspoon; UK/metric teaspoons are sometimes rounded to 5 mL exactly, which differs slightly.

name: Tablespoons → mL
description: Converts a volume in US tablespoons to millilitres by multiplying by 14.7868, the number of millilitres in one US tablespoon.
notes: Uses the US customary tablespoon (3 teaspoons); UK/metric tablespoons are sometimes rounded to 15 mL exactly, which differs slightly.

name: Pounds → Ounces
description: Converts a mass in pounds to ounces by multiplying by 16, the number of avoirdupois ounces in one avoirdupois pound.
notes: Uses the avoirdupois pound and ounce, the common units for everyday weight; troy ounces used for precious metals are different.
